examples.en: Some people call the European Middle Ages the Dark Ages.
That country went through a dark age for a long time.
We learned about the dark age in history class.

examples.ko: 전쟁이 끝나면서 길었던 암흑시대도 막을 내렸어요.
examples.en: With the end of the war, the long dark age also came to a close.
That time was a dark age for our family.

examples.ko: 인터넷이 없던 때는 정보의 암흑시대 같았어요.
examples.en: The time before the internet felt like a dark age for information.

explain: 역사에서는 유럽 중세를 가리키기도 하지만, 일상에서는 '힘들고 희망이 없던 시기'를 비유로 말할 때도 많이 써요. 비슷한 말로 '암흑기'가 있어요.
explain_en: In history it can refer to the European Middle Ages, but in daily life it is often used figuratively for a hard, hopeless period. A similar word is '암흑기'.

examples.en: That person got back at me.
Revenge doesn't help at all.
He spread rumors about me as payback.
If you only think about revenge, your heart gets even heavier.

examples.ko: 앙갚음이 무서워서 아무 말도 못 했어요.
examples.en: I was afraid of retaliation, so I couldn't say anything.

examples.ko: 그런 행동은 그냥 앙갚음에 지나지 않아요.
examples.en: That kind of behavior is nothing more than payback.

explain: '복수'와 비슷하지만, 일상에서 당한 일을 그대로 되갚는 느낌으로 쓰는 일이 많아요. 보통 '앙갚음을 하다'나 '앙갚음하다'로 말해요.
explain_en: It is similar to '복수' (revenge), but it often has the feel of paying someone back for something that happened in everyday life. People usually say '앙갚음을 하다' or '앙갚음하다'.

examples.ko: 언젠가 저 사람에게 꼭 앙갚음할 거예요.
examples.en: Someday I will definitely get back at that person.
He got back at the people who had looked down on him.

examples.ko: 너무 화나도 앙갚음하지 말고 그냥 잊어요.
examples.en: Even if you're very angry, don't retaliate; just forget it.

examples.ko: 친구가 놀린 걸 앙갚음하려고 가방을 숨겼어요.
examples.en: To get back at my friend for teasing me, I hid his bag.
I don't know how I should get even.
I'm thinking of a way to get back at my younger sibling.

explain: '~에게 앙갚음하다'처럼 대상 앞에 '에게'를 써요. '되갚다'는 은혜를 갚을 때도 쓰지만, '앙갚음하다'는 나쁜 일을 되돌려 줄 때만 써요.
explain_en: Use '에게' before the target, as in '~에게 앙갚음하다'. '되갚다' can also be used for repaying a kindness, but '앙갚음하다' is only for paying back something bad.

examples.en: Now that it's winter, the branches are very bare.

examples.ko: 감나무의 앙상한 가지 사이로 초가지붕이 보여요.
examples.en: A thatched roof can be seen between the bare branches of the persimmon tree.
I've lost weight lately and my arms have become bony.
A skinny, bony cat was in the alley.

examples.ko: 할머니의 앙상한 손을 잡으니 마음이 아팠어요.
examples.en: Holding my grandmother's bony hand made my heart ache.

examples.ko: 잎이 다 떨어져서 가지만 앙상하게 남았어요.
examples.en: All the leaves fell, and only the bare branches remain.

explain: 잎이 다 떨어진 가지나 살이 빠져 뼈가 드러난 몸처럼, 있어야 할 것이 없어 초라하고 안쓰러운 느낌이에요. 사람에게 쓰면 '말랐다'보다 더 안타까운 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It describes things that lack what they should have, such as branches with no leaves or a body so thin that the bones show, with a pitiful feel. For people it sounds more sorrowful than simply '말랐다' (thin).

en: being like cats and dogs; being on bad terms

examples.en: The two of them are longtime enemies.

examples.ko: 우리 형과 동생은 만나면 앙숙처럼 싸워요.
examples.en: My older brother and younger sibling fight like sworn enemies whenever they meet.

examples.ko: 그 두 회사는 서로 앙숙 관계예요.
examples.en: Those two companies are rivals who hate each other.
Cats and dogs are commonly said to be sworn enemies.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 앙숙이던 친구와 지금은 제일 친해요.
examples.en: I'm now closest with the friend who was my enemy when we were little.

examples.ko: 앙숙 사이였던 두 나라가 드디어 화해했어요.
examples.en: The two countries that had been bitter enemies finally made peace.

explain: 서로 사이가 아주 나쁜 사람이나 집단에 써요. '원수'보다 무겁지 않아서 장난스럽게도 말할 수 있어요. 보통 '앙숙이다', '앙숙 관계'로 써요.
explain_en: It is used for people or groups that get along very badly. It is lighter than '원수' (enemy), so it can also be said playfully. It usually appears as '앙숙이다' or '앙숙 관계'.

examples.en: He holds a grudge against me.
Out of spite, I deliberately pretended not to know.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 앙심이 깊어서 오래 기억해요.
examples.en: That person holds deep grudges and remembers things for a long time.
The look in his eyes, full of spite, was scary.
If you're consumed by spite, you can't do anything.

examples.ko: 해고된 직원이 앙심을 품고 거짓 소문을 냈어요.
examples.en: The fired employee spread false rumors out of spite.

explain: 상대에게 당한 일 때문에 마음속에 남은 미운 마음이고, 되갚아 주고 싶은 생각까지 담겨 있어요. 보통 '앙심을 품다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It is the resentment that stays in your heart because of something someone did to you, often with a wish to get back at them. People usually say '앙심을 품다'.

en: sharp and shrill; fierce (voice or tone)

examples.en: The cat let out a shrill, fierce cry.
That person shouted sharply.
Her voice was so sharp that it was a bit scary.
Please don't snap at me in that sharp tone.
I was surprised when the child talked back so sharply.
The voice on the phone is really sharp.

explain: 목소리, 말투, 태도가 날카롭고 매섭다는 느낌이에요. 좋은 뜻은 아니어서, 사람에게 직접 말하면 기분 나빠할 수 있어요.
explain_en: It describes a voice, tone or attitude that is sharp and biting. It is not a compliment, so saying it to someone's face can upset them.

en: taking care of one's own business; looking after oneself

examples.ko: 남 걱정은 그만하고 본인 앞가림이나 잘하세요.
examples.en: Stop worrying about others and take care of your own business.

examples.ko: 이제 자기 앞가림은 스스로 해야 해요.
examples.en: Now you have to take care of yourself.
I'm worried because my child can't even look after himself.
I got a job and can finally just about support myself.
Before worrying about others, take care of yourself first.
My younger sibling is young but handles things well on their own.

explain: '앞가림을 하다', '앞가림도 못 하다'처럼 자기 일이나 살림을 스스로 해결하는 걸 말해요. '네 앞가림이나 잘해'는 상대가 기분 나쁠 수 있는 말투예요.
explain_en: It is used in forms like '앞가림을 하다' and '앞가림도 못 하다' for handling your own affairs and living on your own. Saying '네 앞가림이나 잘해' can sound rude to the other person.

examples.en: I spilled coffee on the front of my skirt.
I held the front of my hanbok and walked slowly.
The front of my coat is flapping in the strong wind.

examples.ko: 그는 윗옷 앞자락을 여미고 밖으로 나갔어요.
examples.en: He pulled the front of his jacket closed and went outside.

examples.ko: 아이가 울면서 엄마 치마 앞자락에 매달렸어요.
examples.en: The child cried and clung to the front of her mother's skirt.

examples.ko: 비를 맞아서 윗옷 앞자락이 다 젖었어요.
examples.en: I got rained on, and the front of my top is all wet.

explain: 치마, 저고리, 두루마기처럼 늘어지는 옷의 앞쪽 아랫부분을 말해요. 반대말은 '뒷자락'이에요.
explain_en: It refers to the lower front part of hanging garments such as skirts, jeogori and overcoats. The opposite is '뒷자락'.

en: being worried to death; liver and intestines

examples.en: I've heard nothing for days, and I'm worried sick.
Not knowing how my son was, I was worried sick.

examples.ko: 합격 발표를 기다리며 애간장이 녹는 것 같았어요.
examples.en: Waiting for the results, I felt like I was dying of anxiety.
Do you know how anxious I am?

examples.ko: 그 사람은 일부러 애간장을 태우는 것 같아요.
examples.en: It seems like that person is deliberately making me anxious.

examples.ko: 애간장이 다 녹아서 밥도 못 먹겠어요.
examples.en: I'm so anxious that I can't even eat.

explain: 거의 '애간장이 타다', '애간장을 태우다', '애간장이 녹다'처럼 굳어진 표현으로만 써요. 걱정과 초조함이 아주 클 때 쓰는 말이에요.

phrases.example: 그는 연락도 없이 며칠째 가족의 애간장을 태웠어요.
phrases.en: He has kept his family on edge for days without any word.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대를 몹시 걱정하고 초조하게 만든다는 뜻이에요. 내가 걱정할 때는 '애간장이 타다'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means making someone extremely worried and anxious. When you are the one worrying, say '애간장이 타다'.

explain_en: It is almost always used in fixed expressions such as '애간장이 타다', '애간장을 태우다' and '애간장이 녹다'. It describes very strong worry and anxiety.

examples.en: The child begs and begs me to buy a toy.
He begged and pleaded for forgiveness.
No matter how much I begged, the boss wouldn't allow it.
The customer was begging for a discount.
Seeing him beg so desperately made my heart ache.
You don't need to beg like that; I'll help you.

explain: '애걸하다'보다 더 간절하게, 체면도 없이 계속 매달리는 느낌이에요. 같은 말을 되풀이해 강조한 말이라 대화에서도 쓰이지만 약간 과장된 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: Compared with '애걸하다', it feels more desperate, like clinging and pleading without any pride. The repeated sounds add emphasis, so it can sound a little exaggerated even in conversation.

examples.ko: 그는 한 번만 기회를 달라고 애걸했어요.
examples.en: He begged for just one chance.

examples.ko: 저는 애걸하다시피 해서 겨우 사장님을 만났어요.
examples.en: I practically begged and finally managed to meet the boss.

examples.ko: 친구에게 돈을 빌려 달라고 애걸하기는 싫어요.
examples.en: I don't want to beg my friend to lend me money.
No matter how much I begged, the teacher didn't allow it.
The child spoke as if pleading, with tears in his eyes.
You don't need to beg like that.

explain: 글이나 뉴스에서 자주 보이는 딱딱한 말이에요. 대화에서는 '빌다', '매달리다', '사정하다'처럼 말하는 일이 많아요.
explain_en: This is a fairly stiff word often seen in writing and the news. In conversation people often say '빌다', '매달리다' or '사정하다' instead.

examples.en: An innocent person got punished.

examples.ko: 화가 난다고 애꿎은 동생에게 소리치지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't yell at your innocent younger sibling just because you're angry.

examples.ko: 화가 나서 애꿎은 문을 세게 닫고 나갔어요.
examples.en: I was angry, so I slammed the poor door and left.
I got dragged into the fight and was harmed for no reason.
After botching the exam, I took it out on my pencil and snapped it.
That person was misunderstood through no fault of their own.

explain: 거의 '애꿎은 + 명사' 모양으로 쓰고, 잘못이 없는데 화풀이나 피해를 받는 대상을 말해요. '억울하다'는 당한 사람의 감정이고, '애꿎다'는 그 대상이 죄 없이 피해를 본다는 점을 말해요.
explain_en: It is almost always used as '애꿎은 + noun' for something or someone that suffers blame or anger without having done anything wrong. '억울하다' describes the feeling of the person wronged, while '애꿎다' points to the blameless target.

examples.ko: 멀리 떠난 딸을 기다리는 엄마의 애끓는 마음이 느껴졌어요.
examples.en: I could feel the heartbroken longing of the mother waiting for her daughter who left far away.
With no news, I waited in agony.

examples.ko: 애끓는 사연을 듣고 모두 눈물을 흘렸어요.
examples.en: Everyone cried after hearing the heartbreaking story.
At the news that her daughter was ill, the mother was beside herself with worry.
He called his family in an anguished voice.
A heart-wrenching song about parting played on the radio.

explain: 주로 '애끓는 + 명사', '애끓듯' 모양으로 쓰는 문학적인 말이에요. 슬픔, 걱정, 그리움 때문에 속이 타는 느낌이고, 일상 대화에서는 '속이 타다', '마음이 아프다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It is a literary word mostly used as '애끓는 + noun' or '애끓듯'. It conveys inner torment from sorrow, worry or longing; in daily talk people say '속이 타다' or '마음이 아프다'.

examples.en: My son talks like a little old man.
He's ten but acts as mature as an old soul.
My friends call me an old soul.
Don't talk like an old man.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 애늙은이여서 또래와 잘 안 놀아요.
examples.en: That child is an old soul and doesn't play much with kids his age.

examples.ko: 어릴 때부터 애늙은이 소리를 많이 들었어요.
examples.en: I've heard 'old soul' a lot since I was little.

explain: 나이는 어린데 말과 행동이 어른, 특히 노인처럼 느껴지는 아이를 말해요. 칭찬일 수도 있지만 아이답지 않다는 아쉬움이 담길 수도 있어서 말투에 따라 느낌이 달라요.
explain_en: It refers to a young person whose words and behavior feel adult, especially old-fashioned. It can be praise, but it can also carry a note of regret that the child isn't childlike, so the feel depends on the tone.

examples.en: The students mourned their late teacher.

examples.ko: 무덤을 찾는 건 고인을 애도하는 마음에서예요.
examples.en: Visiting a grave comes from a heart that mourns the deceased.
We paid tribute to the deceased with a moment of silence.

examples.ko: 나라 전체가 슬픔 속에서 그분을 애도하고 있어요.
examples.en: The whole country is mourning him in sorrow.
I wore black clothes to show mourning.
I wrote a letter mourning my friend's death.

explain: '고인을 애도하다'처럼 세상을 떠난 사람을 추모하며 슬퍼할 때 써요. 뉴스나 공식적인 자리에서 많이 쓰고, 일상에서는 '명복을 빌다'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It is used as in '고인을 애도하다' when grieving and remembering someone who has passed away. It is common in the news and formal settings; in daily life people also say '명복을 빌다'.

examples.ko: 제 애마는 십 년 된 낡은 소형차예요.
examples.en: My beloved car is an old compact car that is ten years old.
Every weekend I take my trusty car to the sea.

examples.ko: 아버지는 애마를 닦는 데 한 시간이나 써요.
examples.en: My father spends a whole hour washing his prized car.
The knight rode through the forest with his beloved horse.

examples.ko: 애마가 갑자기 시동이 안 걸려서 지각했어요.
examples.en: My trusty car suddenly wouldn't start, so I was late.

examples.ko: 친구가 애마를 빌려줘서 이사를 쉽게 했어요.
examples.en: My friend lent me his beloved car, so the move was easy.

explain: 원래는 아끼는 말(馬)이라는 뜻인데, 요즘 일상 대화에서는 자기가 아끼는 자동차를 장난스럽게 '내 애마'라고 부르는 경우가 더 많아요. 자동차 광고나 기사에서도 자주 보여요. 말을 가리킬 때는 옛날이야기나 역사 이야기에서 주로 나와요.
explain_en: Originally it meant a horse one treasures, but in everyday talk people more often playfully call their beloved car '내 애마'. You will also see it in car ads and news articles. When it means a real horse, it mostly appears in old tales and historical stories.

examples.en: The question is so vague that it's hard to answer.
That person's answers are always vague.

examples.ko: 애매모호한 표현은 오해를 만들 수 있어요.
examples.en: Ambiguous expressions can cause misunderstandings.
The sentences in the contract are written ambiguously.

examples.ko: 좋다고 해야 할지 싫다고 해야 할지 애매모호하네요.
examples.en: I can't tell whether to say I like it or dislike it; it's unclear.

examples.ko: 애매모호하게 말하지 말고 확실히 알려 주세요.
examples.en: Please don't be vague; tell me clearly.

explain: '애매하다'와 '모호하다'를 겹쳐 강조한 느낌이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '애매하다'만 써도 충분히 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It stacks '애매하다' and '모호하다' for emphasis. In everyday conversation, just '애매하다' is natural enough.

examples.ko: 아이가 밥을 안 먹어서 부모를 애먹여요.
examples.en: The child won't eat, so he gives his parents a hard time.
The mischievous puppy gave us a hard time.
Please don't give our team leader too much trouble.

examples.ko: 고장 난 컴퓨터가 계속 저를 애먹여요.
examples.en: The broken computer keeps giving me trouble.
My younger sibling hid on purpose to give me a hard time.

examples.ko: 이 문제는 몇 년째 우리를 애먹이고 있어요.
examples.en: This problem has been troubling us for years.

explain: 내가 고생하는 건 '애먹다', 남이나 어떤 일이 나를 고생시키는 건 '애먹이다'예요. 사람뿐 아니라 고장 난 물건이나 어려운 문제도 주어가 될 수 있어요.
explain_en: '애먹다' is when you suffer yourself, while '애먹이다' is when someone or something causes you trouble. The subject can be a person, a broken object or a hard problem.

en: pain in the neck; source of anxiety; cause of trouble

examples.ko: 쓰지 않는 피아노가 이젠 애물단지가 됐어요.
examples.en: The piano we don't use has now become a burden.
The youngest son is the family's troublemaker.

examples.ko: 인기 없는 신제품이 회사의 애물단지가 됐어요.
examples.en: The unpopular new product has become a headache for the company.
A big sofa is a nuisance in a small house.

examples.ko: 그 낡은 차는 팔지도 못하는 애물단지 신세예요.
examples.en: That old car is a white elephant that I can't even sell.
Land that was once a source of pride has turned into a burden.

explain: '골칫거리'와 비슷하지만, 버리거나 없애기도 마땅치 않은 물건이나 일에 자주 써요. 사람에게 쓰면 무례하게 들릴 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is similar to '골칫거리' (a headache), but is often used for things you can't easily throw away or get rid of. Using it about a person can sound rude.

examples.ko: 이 시계는 아버지가 남겨 주신 애장품이에요.
examples.en: This watch is a treasured item my father left me.

examples.ko: 제 애장품 1호는 어릴 때 받은 곰 인형이에요.
examples.en: My number one treasured item is a teddy bear I got as a child.
The museum is exhibiting a famous writer's treasured belongings.
The singer put her prized belongings up for auction.
I store my treasured item carefully in case it gets damaged.

examples.ko: 만화책은 제 소중한 애장품 중 하나예요.
examples.en: Comic books are one of my precious belongings.

explain: 내가 특별히 아끼는 물건을 말해요. '소장품'은 모아서 가지고 있는 물건이고, '애장품'은 아끼는 마음이 더 들어간 말이에요.
explain_en: It refers to an item you particularly cherish. '소장품' is something you own in a collection, while '애장품' carries more of a feeling of affection.

examples.en: That teacher cherished me as a favorite student.
He is a famous painter's favorite student.
It's an honor to be called the teacher's favorite student.
The professor sent his favorite student abroad to study.

examples.ko: 애제자가 큰 상을 받아서 스승님이 기뻐하셨어요.
examples.en: The master was delighted that his favorite student won a big prize.

examples.ko: 저는 선생님 애제자는 아니었지만 많이 배웠어요.
examples.en: I wasn't the teacher's favorite student, but I learned a lot.

explain: 스승이 특별히 아끼는 제자를 말해요. 스승이 제자를 소개할 때 자연스럽고, 자기 입으로 '저는 애제자예요'라고 하면 자랑처럼 들릴 수 있어요.
explain_en: It refers to a student a teacher particularly cherishes. It sounds natural when others or the teacher say it, but calling yourself '애제자' can sound like bragging.

examples.en: My grandmother dotes on her youngest grandson.
That bag is something my father treasured.
My parents dote on me so much that it feels like a burden.
I carefully wiped my new camera as if it were a treasure.
I gave my younger sibling the doll I had cherished so much.

examples.ko: 제가 애지중지해서 키운 화분이 꽃을 피웠어요.
examples.en: The potted plant I raised with so much care has bloomed.

explain: '아끼다'보다 더 아주 소중히 다루는 느낌이고, 사람과 물건에 모두 써요. '애지중지 키우다'처럼 '애지중지'만 부사처럼 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It feels stronger than '아끼다', meaning to handle something with great care, and it works for both people and objects. '애지중지' alone is also used like an adverb, as in '애지중지 키우다'.

examples.en: My father is a well-known devoted husband.

examples.ko: 그는 아내 말이라면 뭐든 들어주는 애처가예요.
examples.en: He is a doting husband who does whatever his wife says.

examples.ko: 애처가로 유명한 배우가 아내에게 꽃을 선물했어요.
examples.en: The actor, famous as a devoted husband, gave his wife flowers.
My husband is devoted to me, so he helps with all the housework.

examples.ko: 남자 친구가 나중에 애처가가 될 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think my boyfriend will be a devoted husband later on.
Thanks to my devoted husband, I'm always happy.

explain: 아내를 아끼고 사랑하는 남편을 말해요. 아내를 무서워하는 남편을 뜻하는 '공처가'와 헷갈리지 마세요. 일상에서는 '아내 바보'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It refers to a husband who cherishes and loves his wife. Don't confuse it with '공처가', a husband who is afraid of his wife. In daily talk people also say '아내 바보'.

en: joy and sorrow; happiness and sadness

examples.en: This drama portrays the joys and sorrows of ordinary people.
The market holds the joys and sorrows of its people.
You can feel the immigrants' joys and sorrows in the song.
My grandfather told me about the joys and sorrows of his life.
It's a film about the joys and sorrows of taxi drivers.
The subway holds the joys and sorrows of commuting office workers.

explain: 기쁨과 슬픔이 섞인 삶의 모습을 말하고, '서민의 애환', '삶의 애환'처럼 자주 써요. 대화보다 방송, 기사, 글에서 더 많이 보여요.
explain_en: It describes life where joy and sorrow are mixed together, and often appears as '서민의 애환' or '삶의 애환'. You see it more in broadcasts, articles and writing than in conversation.

en: avoiding greater misfortune with lesser sacrifice

examples.en: I tripped on the street, but I'll think of it as getting my bad luck out of the way.
Think of this accident as a small price paid to ward off worse luck.

examples.ko: 시험 전에 지갑을 잃어버린 게 액땜이면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I hope losing my wallet before the exam is the small bad luck that spares me a bigger one.

examples.ko: 컵을 깬 걸 액땜으로 치기로 했어요.
examples.en: I decided to count breaking the cup as my bit of bad luck out of the way.

examples.ko: 액땜 한번 크게 했으니 이제 잘될 거예요.
examples.en: You've had your share of bad luck, so things will go well now.

examples.ko: 이사 전에 작은 사고가 난 건 액땜일 거예요.
examples.en: The small accident before the move must be a bit of bad luck to ward off worse.

explain: 작은 나쁜 일을 겪어서 큰 불행을 막았다고 위로하는 말이에요. 보통 '액땜했다고 생각해'처럼 나쁜 일이 생긴 뒤에 말해요.
explain_en: It is a comforting idea that a small misfortune has spared you from a bigger one. People usually say things like '액땜했다고 생각해' after something bad happens.

examples.ko: 그 사람 말을 액면 그대로 믿으면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't take that person's words at face value.
It's a problem if you take a joke literally.
I checked the face amount of the check at the bank.
This bond was sold for less than its face value.

examples.ko: 칭찬을 액면 그대로 듣지 말고 속뜻을 생각해요.
examples.en: Don't take the compliment at face value; think about what it really means.

examples.ko: 액면 그대로 번역하면 이상한 문장이 돼요.
examples.en: If you translate it literally, it becomes a strange sentence.

explain: 일상에서는 거의 '액면 그대로'라는 말로 만나요. 돈이나 증권에서는 겉에 적힌 금액을 뜻하지만, 말에서는 겉으로 드러난 의미를 가리켜요.

phrases.example: 그 말을 액면 그대로 받아들이지 마세요.
phrases.en: Don't take those words at face value.
phrases.nuance_ko: 속뜻이나 사정은 따지지 않고 겉으로 드러난 말 그대로라는 뜻이에요. 보통 '받아들이다', '믿다', '해석하다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means taking things exactly as they appear, without considering hidden meanings or circumstances. It usually goes with '받아들이다', '믿다' or '해석하다'.

explain_en: In daily life you mostly meet it in the phrase '액면 그대로'. For money and securities it means the amount printed on the surface, and for words it points to the surface meaning.
